sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ ekapādasthite dharme yatrakvacanagāmini kathaṃ kartavyam asmābhir bhagavaṃs tad vadasva naḥ
english: The gods said: When dharma stands upon a single foot, ranging wherever it will, how then must we conduct ourselves? Tell us this, O Blessed One.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca yatra vedāś ca yajñāś ca tapaḥ satyaṃ damas tathā ahiṃsādharmasaṃyuktāḥ pracareyuḥ surottamāḥ sa vai deśaḥ sevitavyo mā vo 'dharmaḥ padā spṛśet
english: The Blessed Lord said: Where the Vedas and the sacrifices, austerity, truth, and self-restraint flourish, joined to the dharma of non-injury, O best of gods — that is the country you must dwell in, lest unrighteousness so much as touch you with its foot.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca te 'nuśiṣṭā bhagavatā devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tathā namaskṛtvā bhagavate jagmur deśān yathepsitān
english: Vyāsa said: Thus instructed by the Blessed Lord, the gods together with the throngs of seers bowed in homage to him and departed, each to the regions of his desire.

sanskrit: gateṣu tridivaukaḥsu brahmaikaḥ paryavasthitaḥ didṛkṣur bhagavantaṃ tam aniruddhatanau sthitam
english: When the dwellers of the triple heaven had gone, Brahmā alone remained standing there, longing to behold that Blessed Lord abiding in the form of Aniruddha.

sanskrit: taṃ devo darśayām āsa kṛtvā hayaśiro mahat sāṅgān āvartayan vedān kamaṇḍalugaṇitradhṛk
english: The God showed himself to him, having made his great horse-head, chanting the Vedas with their auxiliary lore, and bearing the water-pot and the prayer-beads.

sanskrit: tato 'śvaśirasaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ devam amitaujasam lokakartā prabhur brahmā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Then, beholding that horse-headed God of measureless might, the lord Brahmā, maker of worlds, moved by his wish for the welfare of the worlds —

sanskrit: mūrdhnā praṇamya varadaṃ tasthau prāñjalir agrataḥ sa pariṣvajya devena vacanaṃ śrāvitas tadā
english: — bowed his head before the giver of boons and stood before him with hands joined. The God embraced him, and then he was made to hear these words:

sanskrit: lokakāryagatīḥ sarvās tvaṃ cintaya yathāvidhi dhātā tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvaṃ prabhur jagato guruḥ tvayy āveśitabhāro 'haṃ dhṛtiṃ prāpsyāmy athāñjasā
english: Take thought, as is fitting, of all the courses of the world's business. You are the ordainer of all beings, you are the lord, the teacher of the universe. With the burden laid upon you, I shall at once attain my repose.

sanskrit: yadā ca surakāryaṃ te aviṣahyaṃ bhaviṣyati prādurbhāvaṃ gamiṣyāmi tadātmajñānadeśikaḥ
english: And whenever some task of the gods shall prove beyond your bearing, I shall come forth into manifestation, the guide who imparts knowledge of the Self.

sanskrit: evam uktvā hayaśirās tatraivāntaradhīyata tenānuśiṣṭo brahmāpi svaṃ lokam acirād gataḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the Horse-headed One vanished on that very spot; and Brahmā too, instructed by him, soon departed to his own world.

sanskrit: evam eṣa mahābhāgaḥ padmanābhaḥ sanātanaḥ yajñeṣv agraharaḥ prokto yajñadhārī ca nityadā
english: Thus this most blessed one, the lotus-naveled Eternal One, is declared to be the first receiver of offerings in the sacrifices, and forever the upholder of sacrifice.

sanskrit: nivṛttiṃ cāsthito dharmaṃ gatim akṣayadharmiṇām pravṛttidharmān vidadhe kṛtvā lokasya citratām
english: Established in the dharma of withdrawal — the goal of those whose dharma is imperishable — he yet ordained the dharmas of active engagement, fashioning thereby the manifold variety of the world.

sanskrit: sa ādiḥ sa madhyaḥ sa cāntaḥ prajānāṃ; sa dhātā sa dheyaḥ sa kartā sa kāryam yugānte sa suptaḥ susaṃkṣipya lokān; yugādau prabuddho jagad dhy utsasarja
english: He is the beginning, he the middle, and he the end of all creatures; he is the ordainer and the ordained, the doer and the deed. At the end of an age he sleeps, having drawn the worlds compactly in; at the dawn of an age he wakes and pours forth the world anew.

sanskrit: tasmai namadhvaṃ devāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane ajāya viśvarūpāya dhāmne sarvadivaukasām
english: Bow down to that God, free of the strands yet the very Self of the strands, the unborn, of universal form, the abode of all the dwellers in heaven.

sanskrit: mahābhūtādhipataye rudrāṇāṃ pataye tathā ādityapataye caiva vasūnāṃ pataye tathā
english: To the lord of the great elements, the lord of the Rudras likewise, to the lord of the Ādityas, and to the lord of the Vasus,

sanskrit: aśvibhyāṃ pataye caiva marutāṃ pataye tathā vedayajñādhipataye vedāṅgapataye 'pi ca
english: to the lord of the two Aśvins and the lord of the Maruts, to the lord of the Vedas and their sacrifices, and to the lord of the Vedic sciences —

sanskrit: samudravāsine nityaṃ haraye muñjakeśine śāntaye sarvabhūtānāṃ mokṣadharmānubhāṣiṇe
english: to Hari who dwells forever upon the ocean, whose locks are like muñja-grass; to the peace of all beings, the proclaimer of the dharma of liberation;

sanskrit: tapasāṃ tejasāṃ caiva pataye yaśaso 'pi ca vācaś ca pataye nityaṃ saritāṃ pataye tathā
english: to the lord of austerities and of splendors and of glory, the eternal lord of speech, and likewise the lord of the rivers;

sanskrit: kapardine varāhāya ekaśṛṅgāya dhīmate vivasvate 'śvaśirase caturmūrtidhṛte sadā
english: to the one of matted locks, to the Boar, to the wise One-Horned, to Vivasvat, to the Horse-headed, who bears forever the fourfold form;

sanskrit: guhyāya jñānadṛśyāya akṣarāya kṣarāya ca eṣa devaḥ saṃcarati sarvatragatir avyayaḥ
english: to the hidden one, to him who is seen by knowledge, to the imperishable and to the perishable alike. This God moves abroad, all-pervading in his motion, undecaying.

sanskrit: evam etat purā dṛṣṭaṃ mayā vai jñānacakṣuṣā kathitaṃ tac ca vaḥ sarvaṃ mayā pṛṣṭena tattvataḥ
english: All this I myself beheld of old with the eye of knowledge, and, being asked, I have told it all to you according to the truth.

sanskrit: kriyatāṃ madvacaḥ śiṣyāḥ sevyatāṃ harir īśvaraḥ gīyatāṃ vedaśabdaiś ca pūjyatāṃ ca yathāvidhi
english: Do as my words bid you, O disciples: serve Hari the Lord, sing his praise with the words of the Veda, and worship him as the rite ordains.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktās tu vayaṃ tena vedavyāsena dhīmatā sarve śiṣyāḥ sutaś cāsya śukaḥ paramadharmavit
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the wise Vedavyāsa, we — all his disciples, and his son Śuka, knower of the highest dharma —

sanskrit: sa cāsmākam upādhyāyaḥ sahāsmābhir viśāṃ pate caturvedodgatābhiś ca ṛgbhis tam abhituṣṭuve
english: and our teacher himself together with us, O lord of peoples, hymned that One with verses drawn forth from the four Vedas.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi evaṃ me 'kathayad rājan purā dvaipāyano guruḥ
english: All this that you asked of me I have now declared to you. Even so, O king, did my teacher Dvaipāyana relate it to me of old.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ yaś cedaṃ parikīrtayet namo bhagavate kṛtvā samāhitamanā naraḥ
english: Whoever should constantly hear this, and whoever should proclaim it abroad — a man who, with mind composed, has uttered his homage to the Blessed Lord —

sanskrit: bhavaty arogo dyutimān balarūpasamanvitaḥ āturo mucyate rogād baddho mucyeta bandhanāt
english: becomes free of sickness, radiant, endowed with strength and beauty; the afflicted is released from his ailment, and the bound is freed from his bondage.

sanskrit: kāmakāmī labhet kāmaṃ dīrgham āyur avāpnuyāt brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavedī syāt kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet vaiśyo vipulalābhaḥ syāc chūdraḥ sukham avāpnuyāt
english: He who desires his heart's desire attains it and wins long life: the brāhmaṇa becomes versed in all the Vedas, the kṣatriya becomes victorious, the vaiśya wins abundant gain, and the śūdra attains his ease.

sanskrit: aputro labhate putraṃ kanyā caivepsitaṃ patim lagnagarbhā vimucyeta garbhiṇī janayet sutam vandhyā prasavam āpnoti putrapautrasamṛddhimat
english: The sonless gains a son, and the maiden the husband she has wished for; she whose womb is bound is delivered, the pregnant woman bears a son, and the barren attains a fruitful birth, rich in sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: kṣemeṇa gacched adhvānam idaṃ yaḥ paṭhate pathi yo yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate sa tam āpnoti ca dhruvam
english: He who recites this upon the road shall journey his way in safety; and whatever desire a man desires, that he surely attains.

sanskrit: idaṃ maharṣer vacanaṃ viniścitaṃ; mahātmanaḥ puruṣavarasya kīrtanam samāgamaṃ carṣidivaukasām imaṃ; niśamya bhaktāḥ susukhaṃ labhante
english: This is the assured word of the great seer, the proclamation of the great-souled, supreme Person; and the faithful, having heard this assembly of the seers and the dwellers of heaven, attain the highest bliss.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca astauṣīd yair imaṃ vyāsaḥ saśiṣyo madhusūdanam nāmabhir vividhair eṣāṃ niruktaṃ bhagavan mama
english: Janamejaya said: With what manifold names did Vyāsa together with his disciples hymn this slayer of Madhu? Their derivation, O Blessed One, is what I would have.

sanskrit: vaktum arhasi śuśrūṣoḥ prajāpatipater hareḥ śrutvā bhaveyaṃ yat pūtaḥ śaraccandra ivāmalaḥ
english: You should declare to me, who long to hear it, the names of Hari, the lord of the lords of creatures, that, having heard them, I may become pure and spotless as the autumn moon.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇu rājan yathācaṣṭa phalgunasya harir vibhuḥ prasannātmātmano nāmnāṃ niruktaṃ guṇakarmajam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hear, O king, how the all-pervading Hari, his Self made gracious, declared to Phalguna the derivation of his own names, born of his qualities and his deeds.

sanskrit: nāmabhiḥ kīrtitais tasya keśavasya mahātmanaḥ pṛṣṭavān keśavaṃ rājan phalgunaḥ paravīrahā
english: Concerning the names already proclaimed of that great-souled Keśava, Phalguna, slayer of the heroes of the foe, put his question to Keśava, O king.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bhagavan bhūtabhavyeśa sarvabhūtasṛg avyaya lokadhāma jagannātha lokānām abhayaprada
english: Arjuna said: O Blessed Lord, ruler of what has been and what shall be, undecaying maker of all beings, abode of the worlds, master of the universe, giver of fearlessness to the worlds —

sanskrit: yāni nāmāni te deva kīrtitāni maharṣibhiḥ vedeṣu sapurāṇeṣu yāni guhyāni karmabhiḥ
english: those names of yours, O God, that are proclaimed by the great seers in the Vedas and the Purāṇas, and those that are kept secret, derived from your deeds —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ niruktaṃ tvatto 'haṃ śrotum icchāmi keśava na hy anyo vartayen nāmnāṃ niruktaṃ tvām ṛte prabho
english: their derivation I wish to hear from you, Keśava; for no other than you, O Lord, could expound the derivation of these names.

sanskrit: śrībhagavān uvāca ṛgvede sayajurvede tathaivātharvasāmasu purāṇe sopaniṣade tathaiva jyotiṣe 'rjuna
english: The Blessed Lord said: In the Ṛgveda with the Yajurveda, and likewise in the Atharva and the Sāma, in the Purāṇa together with the Upaniṣads, and so too in the lore of the heavenly lights, O Arjuna,

sanskrit: sāṃkhye ca yogaśāstre ca āyurvede tathaiva ca bahūni mama nāmāni kīrtitāni maharṣibhiḥ
english: and in the Sāṃkhya and the science of Yoga, and in the Āyurveda as well — many are the names of mine that the great seers have proclaimed.

sanskrit: gauṇāni tatra nāmāni karmajāni ca kāni cit niruktaṃ karmajānāṃ ca śṛṇuṣva prayato 'nagha kathyamānaṃ mayā tāta tvaṃ hi me 'rdhaṃ smṛtaḥ purā
english: Among these, some names are figurative and some are born of my deeds. Hear now, with attentive devotion, O sinless one, the derivation of those born of deeds, as I tell it, dear friend — for you of old are remembered as the half of me.

sanskrit: namo 'tiyaśase tasmai dehināṃ paramātmane nārāyaṇāya viśvāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane
english: Homage to that one of surpassing glory, the supreme Self of all embodied beings, to Nārāyaṇa, the All, free of the strands yet the very Self of the strands.

sanskrit: yasya prasādajo brahmā rudraś ca krodhasaṃbhavaḥ yo 'sau yonir hi sarvasya sthāvarasya carasya ca
english: From whose grace Brahmā was born, and Rudra from whose wrath came into being — who is the very womb of all that is, whether unmoving or moving.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśaguṇaṃ yat tat sattvaṃ sattvavatāṃ vara prakṛtiḥ sā parā mahyaṃ rodasī yogadhāriṇī ṛtā satyāmarājayyā lokānām ātmasaṃjñitā
english: That essence which possesses the eighteen attributes, O best of the steadfast — that is the supreme Nature belonging to me, the sustainer of heaven and earth through yoga, the ordered Truth, unconquerable by the immortals, named the Self of the worlds.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvāḥ pravartante sargapralayavikriyāḥ tato yajñaś ca yaṣṭā ca purāṇaḥ puruṣo virāṭ aniruddha iti prokto lokānāṃ prabhavāpyayaḥ
english: From it proceed all the transformations of creation and dissolution; thence come the sacrifice and the sacrificer. The ancient Person, the Cosmic Vast, is declared Aniruddha, the origin and the ending of the worlds.

sanskrit: brāhme rātrikṣaye prāpte tasya hy amitatejasaḥ prasādāt prādurabhavat padmaṃ padmanibhekṣaṇa tatra brahmā samabhavat sa tasyaiva prasādajaḥ
english: When the night of Brahmā reached its close, by the grace of that one of measureless splendor there appeared a lotus, O you whose eyes are like the lotus; and there Brahmā came into being, himself the offspring of that grace.

sanskrit: ahnaḥ kṣaye lalāṭāc ca suto devasya vai tathā krodhāviṣṭasya saṃjajñe rudraḥ saṃhārakārakaḥ
english: And at the close of the day, from the forehead of the God, possessed by wrath, there was born his son Rudra, the worker of destruction.

sanskrit: etau dvau vibudhaśreṣṭhau prasādakrodhajau smṛtau tadādeśitapanthānau sṛṣṭisaṃhārakārakau nimittamātraṃ tāv atra sarvaprāṇivarapradau
english: These two, foremost among the wise, are remembered as born of grace and of wrath, treading the path he appointed, the makers of creation and destruction; yet here they are but the instrumental cause, those givers of boons to all living things.

sanskrit: kapardī jaṭilo muṇḍaḥ śmaśānagṛhasevakaḥ ugravratadharo rudro yogī tripuradāruṇaḥ
english: Of braided crest, matted-haired, or shaven; haunter of the burning-ground as his home; bearer of fierce vows is Rudra, the yogin, terrible to the Triple City.

sanskrit: dakṣakratuharaś caiva bhaganetraharas tathā nārāyaṇātmako jñeyaḥ pāṇḍaveya yuge yuge
english: Destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, and despoiler of Bhaga's eyes — he is to be known, O son of Pāṇḍu, as having Nārāyaṇa for his very Self, age after age.

sanskrit: tasmin hi pūjyamāne vai devadeve maheśvare saṃpūjito bhavet pārtha devo nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ
english: For when that God of gods, Maheśvara, is worshipped, then, O Pārtha, the lord God Nārāyaṇa is worshipped too.

sanskrit: aham ātmā hi lokānāṃ viśvānāṃ pāṇḍunandana tasmād ātmānam evāgre rudraṃ saṃpūjayāmy aham
english: For I am the Self of all the worlds, O delight of Pāṇḍu; and therefore it is my own Self, as Rudra, that I worship first of all.

sanskrit: yady ahaṃ nārcayeyaṃ vai īśānaṃ varadaṃ śivam ātmānaṃ nārcayet kaś cid iti me bhāvitaṃ manaḥ mayā pramāṇaṃ hi kṛtaṃ lokaḥ samanuvartate
english: Were I not to worship Īśāna, the boon-giving Śiva, then no one would worship the Self — so has my mind reflected. For the standard is set by me, and the world follows after.

sanskrit: pramāṇāni hi pūjyāni tatas taṃ pūjayāmy aham yas taṃ vetti sa māṃ vetti yo 'nu taṃ sa hi mām anu
english: For what serves as a standard must be honored; therefore do I worship him. He who knows him knows me, and he who follows after him follows after me.

sanskrit: rudro nārāyaṇaś caiva sattvam ekaṃ dvidhākṛtam loke carati kaunteya vyaktisthaṃ sarvakarmasu
english: Rudra and Nārāyaṇa are one single essence made twofold, that moves through the world, O son of Kuntī, present in manifest form in all its works.

sanskrit: na hi me kena cid deyo varaḥ pāṇḍavanandana iti saṃcintya manasā purāṇaṃ viśvam īśvaram putrārtham ārādhitavān ātmānam aham ātmanā
english: There is none from whom a boon need be granted to me, O delight of the Pāṇḍavas; yet, reflecting thus in mind, for the sake of a son I propitiated the ancient Lord of the universe — my own Self, by my own self.

sanskrit: na hi viṣṇuḥ praṇamati kasmai cid vibudhāya tu ṛta ātmānam eveti tato rudraṃ bhajāmy aham
english: For Viṣṇu bows down to no god whatsoever, save to his own Self alone; and therefore it is Rudra that I revere.

sanskrit: sabrahmakāḥ sarudrāś ca sendrā devāḥ saharṣibhiḥ arcayanti suraśreṣṭhaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim
english: The gods, with Brahmā, with Rudra, with Indra, and with the seers, all worship the God Nārāyaṇa, Hari, the best of the celestials.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyatāṃ vartatāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ caiva bhārata sarveṣām agraṇīr viṣṇuḥ sevyaḥ pūjyaś ca nityaśaḥ
english: Of all beings yet to come and of those now present, O Bhārata, Viṣṇu is the foremost, ever to be served and ever to be worshipped.

sanskrit: namasva havyadaṃ viṣṇuṃ tathā śaraṇadaṃ nama varadaṃ namasva kaunteya havyakavyabhujaṃ nama
english: Bow to Viṣṇu, the giver of oblations; bow likewise to the giver of refuge; bow to the giver of boons, O son of Kuntī; bow to him who consumes the offerings to gods and to ancestors.

sanskrit: caturvidhā mama janā bhaktā evaṃ hi te śrutam teṣām ekāntinaḥ śreṣṭhās te caivānanyadevatāḥ aham eva gatis teṣāṃ nirāśīḥkarmakāriṇām
english: Of four kinds are my devoted people, as you have heard; among them the single-minded are the best, those who hold to no other deity. I alone am the goal of those who act without craving for reward.

sanskrit: ye ca śiṣṭās trayo bhaktāḥ phalakāmā hi te matāḥ sarve cyavanadharmāṇaḥ pratibuddhas tu śreṣṭhabhāk
english: And the remaining three kinds of devotees are accounted as desirous of reward; all of them are of a nature that falls away, save that the awakened one wins the better portion.

sanskrit: brahmāṇaṃ śitikaṇṭhaṃ ca yāś cānyā devatāḥ smṛtāḥ prabuddhavaryāḥ sevante mām evaiṣyanti yat param bhaktaṃ prati viśeṣas te eṣa pārthānukīrtitaḥ
english: Those eminent among the awakened who serve Brahmā and the Blue-throated and whatever other deities are remembered, shall come to me, the supreme. This distinction among devotees, O Pārtha, has now been declared to you.

sanskrit: tvaṃ caivāhaṃ ca kaunteya naranārāyaṇau smṛtau bhārāvataraṇārthaṃ hi praviṣṭau mānuṣīṃ tanum
english: You and I, O son of Kuntī, are remembered as Nara and Nārāyaṇa, who for the sake of lightening the earth's burden have entered into human form.

sanskrit: jānāmy adhyātmayogāṃś ca yo 'haṃ yasmāc ca bhārata nivṛttilakṣaṇo dharmas tathābhyudayiko 'pi ca
english: I know the disciplines of the inner Self, and who I am and whence, O Bhārata — both the dharma marked by withdrawal and the dharma that leads to worldly flourishing.

sanskrit: narāṇām ayanaṃ khyātam aham ekaḥ sanātanaḥ āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ ayanaṃ mama tat pūrvam ato nārāyaṇo hy aham
english: The refuge of men is renowned; I alone am the Eternal. The waters are declared to be 'nāra,' for the waters are indeed the offspring of Nara; they were of old my resting-place, and therefore I am Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: chādayāmi jagad viśvaṃ bhūtvā sūrya ivāṃśubhiḥ sarvabhūtādhivāsaś ca vāsudevas tato hy aham
english: I overspread the whole universe, becoming like the sun with its rays; and I am the dwelling-place of all beings — therefore am I Vāsudeva.

sanskrit: gatiś ca sarvabhūtānāṃ prajānāṃ cāpi bhārata vyāptā me rodasī pārtha kāntiś cābhyadhikā mama
english: I am the goal of all beings and of all creatures, O Bhārata; heaven and earth are pervaded by me, O Pārtha, and surpassing is my radiance.

sanskrit: adhibhūtāni cānte 'haṃ tad icchaṃś cāsmi bhārata kramaṇāc cāpy ahaṃ pārtha viṣṇur ity abhisaṃjñitaḥ
english: At the end I overspread the elements, and I am so by my own will, O Bhārata; and because of my striding forth, O Pārtha, I am named Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: damāt siddhiṃ parīpsanto māṃ janāḥ kāmayanti hi divaṃ corvīṃ ca madhyaṃ ca tasmād dāmodaro hy aham
english: Through self-restraint men seek perfection, and so they yearn for me; and because I encompass heaven, earth, and the region between as with a girdle, therefore am I Dāmodara.

sanskrit: pṛśnir ity ucyate cānnaṃ vedā āpo 'mṛtaṃ tathā mamaitāni sadā garbhe pṛśnigarbhas tato hy aham
english: Food is called 'pṛśni,' and so too the Vedas, the waters, and the nectar of immortality; these are forever within my womb — therefore am I Pṛśnigarbha.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaḥ prāhur evaṃ māṃ tritakūpābhipātitam pṛśnigarbha tritaṃ pāhīty ekatadvitapātitam
english: Thus the seers called upon me, when Trita had been cast into the well by Ekata and Dvita: 'O Pṛśnigarbha, save Trita who has been hurled down!'

sanskrit: tataḥ sa brahmaṇaḥ putra ādyo ṛṣivaras tritaḥ uttatārodapānād vai pṛśnigarbhānukīrtanāt
english: Then that Trita, the firstborn son of Brahmā, the best of seers, climbed up out of the well, by the very proclaiming of Pṛśnigarbha's name.

sanskrit: sūryasya tapato lokān agneḥ somasya cāpy uta aṃśavo ye prakāśante mama te keśasaṃjñitāḥ sarvajñāḥ keśavaṃ tasmān mām āhur dvijasattamāḥ
english: The rays that shine forth from the sun as it scorches the worlds, and from fire and from the moon, are mine, and are called my locks (keśa); therefore the all-knowing, the most excellent of the twice-born, call me Keśava.

sanskrit: svapatnyām āhito garbha utathyena mahātmanā utathye 'ntarhite caiva kadā cid devamāyayā bṛhaspatir athāvindat tāṃ patnīṃ tasya bhārata
english: A child had been begotten in his own wife by the great-souled Utathya; and once, when Utathya had vanished from sight through the gods' enchantment, Bṛhaspati found that wife of his, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato vai tam ṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ maithunopagataṃ tathā uvāca garbhaḥ kaunteya pañcabhūtasamanvitaḥ
english: Then, O son of Kuntī, the child within the womb, already endowed with the five elements, spoke thus to that best of seers as he came to the act of union:

sanskrit: pūrvāgato 'haṃ varada nārhasy ambāṃ prabādhitum etad bṛhaspatiḥ śrutvā cukrodha ca śaśāpa ca
english: 'I have come here before you, O giver of boons; you ought not to trouble my mother.' Hearing this, Bṛhaspati grew wrathful and pronounced a curse.

sanskrit: maithunopagato yasmāt tvayāhaṃ vinivāritaḥ tasmād andho jāsyasi tvaṃ macchāpān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: 'Since you have turned me back as I came to the act of union, therefore you shall be born blind by my curse — herein is no doubt.'

sanskrit: sa śāpād ṛṣimukhyasya dīrghaṃ tama upeyivān sa hi dīrghatamā nāma nāmnā hy āsīd ṛṣiḥ purā
english: By the curse of that chief of seers he passed into long darkness; and so that seer was of old known by the name Dīrghatamas, 'Long-Darkness.'

sanskrit: vedān avāpya caturaḥ sāṅgopāṅgān sanātanān prayojayām āsa tadā nāma guhyam idaṃ mama
english: Having mastered the four eternal Vedas with their primary and secondary auxiliaries, he then made use of this secret name of mine.
